extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIGMS/NIH grant applications (faculty and investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for crafting a strong NIGMS/NIH grant application covering planning, writing quality, structure, seeking feedback, contacting program officers, and available webinar resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Start early with your application; develop a schedule to reach writing milestones, including time for reading, writing, receiving peer feedback, and revising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes allocating explicit time for each stage (reading, drafting, peer review, revision) so the application is not rushed. Planning early helps accommodate iterative feedback and improves polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality — clear paragraph-level structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a clear topic sentence for each paragraph with one main point or idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each paragraph should communicate a single, easily identifiable idea via a strong topic sentence to improve readability and reviewer comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality — sentence clarity and background
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to keep sentences as clear, simple, and short as possible; include enough background information to enable the reader to understand your proposed work; spell out acronyms and minimize jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize plain, concise sentences and sufficient context so reviewers both inside and outside your immediate subfield can follow the rationale. Avoid unexplained acronyms and discipline-specific jargon to increase accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structuring your application
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a clear, organized structure with headings; use short paragraphs, bulleted or numbered lists, adequate white space, and indents; use bold text judiciously to highlight key concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Layout and visual cues (headings, lists, white space, selective bolding) improve scannability and help reviewers locate major points quickly. Avoid dense blocks of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting feedback / pre-submission peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider asking your peers to be pre-readers — mentors, collaborators, experienced investigators in your organization, or colleagues elsewhere; if possible, have both experts in your field and those who are less familiar with your science provide feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of expert and non-expert readers to catch technical weaknesses and clarity issues. Include mentors and experienced investigators to review for competitiveness and compliance with expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting NIGMS program officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you apply, strongly get advice from a program officer relevant to your area of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officers can advise on fit to funding opportunities, appropriate scope, and strategic tips — contact them early in the planning process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available NIGMS resources
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS recommends reviewing their grant writing webinar series, which discusses faculty readiness and submission considerations; determining whether a funding opportunity is right for you; and writing a competitive application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage agency-provided webinars and guidance materials to understand readiness, select appropriate FOAs, and learn best practices for competitive applications.
